Tareekh: guide

Case diary for advocates · district courts, High Courts, Supreme Court

Features · Screen guide · Download

Features

Tareekh is a case diary for advocates on Android: your cases, next dates, orders, reminders and cause lists in one place, working with the public pages of eCourts, the High Courts and the Supreme Court. You type every CAPTCHA; everything else is done for you.

Your cases in one place

  • Add a case by hand, by typing it the way you write it (e.g. TS 245/2026 Baruipur), or from a document.
  • Upload or share a summons, order, notice, plaint or eCourts screenshot: the phone reads it (PDFs up to 3 pages) and fills in court, case type, number, year, hearing date and parties.
  • Screenshots of tables (like the eCourts app's case lists) are read column by column.
  • If a detail is missing you are told, and can fill it in or save as it is.
  • You choose whose name the case is saved under (petitioner, respondent or your client), with the case number or the name only.
  • Import your whole eCourts app 'My Cases' export (district and High Court) in one step; imported again, cases are updated, not duplicated.

Next dates, found for you

  • At 6:30 pm Tareekh reminds you to check the day's hearings; for two more days it keeps asking until eCourts shows the new date.
  • Check on eCourts opens the court's own page already filled in; you type only the CAPTCHA.
  • The next date, stage, judge, parties, acts and full hearing history are read and saved.
  • If eCourts is down or late, enter the date yourself (manual override).
  • A clear message when a court site is not available, with Try again.

Court orders, filed per case

  • Every order uploaded on eCourts is downloaded when you open the case there.
  • Saved in Download/Tareekh/Orders/<client name> <case number>/, one folder per case, named by date.
  • Opened, shared on WhatsApp, and kept even if the app is removed.
  • Only new orders are fetched; nothing is downloaded twice.

Reminders and calendar

  • Every hearing goes into your Google Calendar with alerts 2 days before and at 8 am.
  • 8 am: today's matters; 8 pm: tomorrow's matters.
  • 2 days before: a reminder with 'Send WhatsApp reminder' for the client.
  • 3 days before: a fee reminder for clients whose fee is not marked paid.
  • Month calendar with the number of matters each day, and a warning when two courts clash.

Your clients

  • One-tap Call, WhatsApp and Save contact; the contact name is the client's name followed by the case number.
  • WhatsApp reminder to the client with the case, court, date and purpose typed in your own words; you tap Send.
  • If no number is saved, Tareekh asks for it once and keeps it with the case.

Courts across India

  • District courts of every state: state, district and court complex from eCourts' own lists.
  • All 25 High Courts and their 44 benches (Appellate Side, Original Side, circuit benches) on their own eCourts pages.
  • Case types of every High Court built in (WPA, CRR, CRM(A), FMA…), so a paper that shows only 'WPA 12345 of 2024' is recognised.
  • Supreme Court case status and cause lists.

Cause lists

  • High Court, district court and Supreme Court cause lists for yesterday, today, tomorrow or any date.
  • High Court lists open by themselves (no CAPTCHA); Tareekh says if nothing is published yet.
  • Cause list PDFs are saved in Download/Tareekh/Cause lists.

Notes

  • Notes on their own or linked to a case, with a reminder date and time.
  • Today, Tomorrow, Checks due and Fees due at a glance on the first screen.

Your data, your phone

  • Everything is stored on your phone; nothing is sent anywhere except to the court sites you open.
  • Export a backup (cases, notes) to Google Drive; import it on a new phone.
  • Light and dark mode; reminders keep working after the phone restarts.

Getting started

  • Install the Tareekh APK on the phone and open it.
  • Tap Allow for notifications and calendar, and let Tareekh run in the background (battery: Unrestricted).
  • Add cases: import your eCourts app My Cases export (Settings › Import), upload documents, or type them.
  • For a faster eCourts: on the phone, Settings › Network › Private DNS › dns.google.
See the screen guide for a picture of every screen, with arrows explaining each part.

Download

  • Tareekh 2.0 for Android: the APK is attached to the latest release of this repository (Releases › Tareekh-2.0.apk). Install it on the phone and allow installs from that source once.
  • This guide as PDF: Tareekh-Screen-Guide.pdf and Tareekh-Features.pdf in the same folder.

Screen guide

Every screen of Tareekh, as it looks on an Android phone. The numbered arrows point at each part of the screen; the list beside each picture explains it. The cases shown are made-up examples.

1 · Notes: your day at a glance

The first tab. It opens every time you start Tareekh.

  1. 1
    Today / Tomorrow

    How many matters are fixed today and tomorrow. Tap to open them in Cases.

  2. 2
    Checks due

    Hearings that have happened and whose next date is not yet known. Each needs a quick check on eCourts.

  3. 3
    Fees due

    Clients with a hearing in the next 3 days whose fee is not marked paid (only cases with a phone number).

  4. 4
    Check

    Opens eCourts for that case with everything filled in; you type the CAPTCHA, the new date is saved.

  5. 5
    WhatsApp (fees)

    Opens the client's WhatsApp with a polite fee reminder already typed.

  6. 6
    Notes

    Your own notes. A note can have a reminder (alarm) and can be linked to a case. Tick it when done.

  7. 7
    New note

    Write a note, set a reminder date and time, or link it to a case.

2 · Cases: every matter, by date

All your cases, with a month calendar of hearings.

  1. 1
    Search

    Type any part of a name, number, court or place to find a case.

  2. 2
    Court filter

    Show all courts, or only District, High Court or Supreme Court cases.

  3. 3
    By date / All / Disposed

    By date shows the calendar and upcoming hearings; All lists everything; Disposed shows closed cases.

  4. 4
    Sync

    Writes every hearing into your phone's Google Calendar (with alerts 2 days before and at 8 am).

  5. 5
    Calendar

    Each day shows how many matters are fixed. Tap a day to see only its cases and your other calendar entries.

  6. 6
    Clash warning

    Warns when you have matters in two different court towns on the same day.

  7. 7
    Add case

    Add a case by hand, or upload a summons, order or screenshot for Tareekh to read.

3 · A case

Tap any case to open it. Everything about the matter is on this one page.

  1. 1
    Next date

    The next hearing date, its purpose and the case stage.

  2. 2
    Check on eCourts

    Opens the court's page filled in (CNR, or case type, number and year). Type the CAPTCHA; the next date, hearings and orders are saved.

  3. 3
    Enter date

    Manual override: type the next date yourself if eCourts is down or late. The calendar is updated too.

  4. 4
    Save contact as

    The name to save your client under in your phone: name first, then the case number. Tap to copy.

  5. 5
    WhatsApp reminder to client

    Opens the client's WhatsApp with the hearing reminder typed (case, court, date). You tap Send.

  6. 6
    Call / WhatsApp / Save

    Call the client, message them, or save them as a phone contact in one tap.

  7. 7
    Fee paid

    Mark the fee as paid so no fee reminder is sent for this date.

  8. 8
    Orders

    Court orders downloaded from eCourts, newest first. Tap to open; the share icon sends it on WhatsApp.

4 · Checking a case on eCourts (example)

What you see after tapping Check on eCourts and typing the CAPTCHA. (Illustration made with a sample page: on the real court site the layout is the court's own.)

  1. 1
    Next date read from the court

    Tareekh reads the next hearing date, stage, judge, parties and hearing history from the page.

  2. 2
    Orders on the page

    Every order listed on the court's page is downloaded into the case's folder: Download/Tareekh/Orders/<client> <case>.

  3. 3
    Saved automatically

    For a case already in your list, the new date and new orders are saved by themselves. You are told how many orders were saved.

  4. 4
    Open the case in Tareekh

    Jump back to the case page. A new case shows 'Save to My Cases (with orders)' here instead.

5 · Adding a case from a document

Upload (or share to Tareekh) a summons, order, notice or eCourts screenshot; PDFs up to 3 pages are read too.

  1. 1
    Found in the document

    What Tareekh read: ✓ means found, – means not found. Check it before saving.

  2. 2
    Case details

    Case type, number, year, court, hearing date and both parties are filled in for you.

  3. 3
    Show document text

    See (and copy) exactly what the phone read, useful if something was read wrongly.

  4. 4
    Edit anything

    Every field can be corrected by hand before you save.

6 · Whose name to save the case under

Asked every time you save a new case.

  1. 1
    Petitioner / respondent

    Choose the party who is your client; the full name is used.

  2. 2
    Another name

    Or type your client's name, e.g. a company contact.

  3. 3
    Name + number / Name only

    Save as 'Name TYPE NO-YEAR' (the name always first) or just the name.

  4. 4
    Saved as

    Preview of the name used for the case, the contact and the orders folder.

7 · When court details are missing

If the document did not give an important detail, Tareekh says so before saving.

  1. 1
    What is missing

    Court, case number or CNR, case type, year, next date or parties: whatever could not be found.

  2. 2
    Save as it is

    Save with what the document gave. You can add the rest later with Edit.

  3. 3
    Fill them in

    Go back to the form and type the missing details now.

8 · Search: district courts

Court-wise search. The kind of court with most of your cases opens first.

  1. 1
    Open eCourts search

    The full eCourts search page (party, advocate, FIR, Act and more).

  2. 2
    Choose court

    Any court in India: state, district and court complex, straight from eCourts' own lists. Recent courts are remembered.

  3. 3
    Find a case

    Type the case as you would write it; Tareekh fills the eCourts form and you type the CAPTCHA.

  4. 4
    Open by CNR

    The quickest search: the 16-character CNR number.

9 · Search: High Courts

All 25 High Courts and their 44 benches, opened on their own eCourts pages.

  1. 1
    High Court

    Choose the High Court; your last choice is remembered.

  2. 2
    Bench / side

    Appellate Side, Original Side, circuit benches: every bench has its own page.

  3. 3
    All searches

    That bench's full eCourts menu (case number, party, advocate, orders, cause list).

  4. 4
    Case number

    WPA, CRR, FMA…: the case type, number and year are filled in; you type the CAPTCHA.

10 · Choosing any court in India

State › district › court complex, with a filter box.

  1. 1
    Where you are

    The state already chosen; next the district, then the court complex.

  2. 2
    Type to filter

    Type a few letters to find a district or court quickly.

  3. 3
    Lists from eCourts

    The lists are read live from eCourts, so every court in India is there.

11 · Cause lists

Today's (or any day's) cause list for a High Court bench, a district court or the Supreme Court.

  1. 1
    Court

    High Court, District court or Supreme Court.

  2. 2
    Bench

    For High Courts, choose the bench or side.

  3. 3
    Yesterday / Today / Tomorrow

    One tap opens the list for that day.

  4. 4
    Any date

    Pick a date from the calendar, then Open.

12 · A High Court cause list

High Court lists open by themselves (no CAPTCHA).

  1. 1
    What was found

    How many lists are published for the date, or 'not published yet'.

  2. 2

13 · WhatsApp reminder without a number

If no phone number is saved for the case.

  1. 1
    Client's number

    Type it once: it is saved with the case.

  2. 2
    Save and open WhatsApp

    Saves the number and opens WhatsApp with the reminder typed; you tap Send.

14 · Reminders on your phone

Tareekh reminds you even when the app is closed.

  1. 1
    2 days before

    Each hearing two days ahead, with the court, purpose and client.

  2. 2

    Opens the client's WhatsApp with the reminder typed (or asks for the number first).

15 · A note with a reminder

From the Notes tab or from any case.

    Note

    Anything you need to remember.

  2. 2
    Link to a case

    The note then also shows on that case's page.

  3. 3
    Reminder

    Pick a date and time; a notification comes then (it opens the case).

16 · Settings

Backup, your WhatsApp wording and the look of the app.

  1. 1
    Export / Import

    Save all cases and notes to a backup file (keep it in Google Drive); Import also reads the eCourts app's My Cases export.

  2. 2
    WhatsApp reminder message

    Your own wording; {client} {case} {court} {date} {purpose} are filled in for each case.

  3. 3
    Appearance

    Phone setting, Light or Dark.

  4. 4
    Court websites

    If a court page keeps showing old results, clear what the built-in browser stored.
